People came and told Jehoshaphat, “A huge army is coming to attack you! They are coming from the region of Edom, on the other side of the Sea of Salt. They have already gotten as far as Hazezon Tamar!” (Another name for that place is Engedi.)
This made Jehoshaphat very afraid. He determined to ask Yahweh what he should do. He commanded everyone in Judah to eat little food {to show how much distress they felt}.
People from Judah gathered in Jerusalem to ask Yahweh to help them. They came from cities throughout Judah to do that.
People from Jerusalem and throughout Judah gathered in the large public courtyard of the temple. Jehoshaphat stood in front of them

and he prayed, “Yahweh, you are the God whom our ancestors worshiped. You are the God who reigns from heaven. You rule over all the different kingdoms on earth. You possess such great power that no one can successfully oppose you.

You, our God, are the one who forced the people who lived in this land to leave so that your Israelite people could live here. {Our ancestor} Abraham was your friend, and you gave this land to him and his descendants forever.
We Israelites have been living here, and we have built a temple for you here where we worship you. When King Solomon dedicated the temple, he prayed,

‘We may experience disasters because you are punishing us. Enemies may attack us, or diseases may spread, or we may not be able to grow enough food. If that happens, since you have promised to be present here, we will assemble at this temple where you are present. We will plead with you to help us, and may you do what we ask and rescue us.’

Here is the problem we now have. You did not allow our Israelite ancestors to enter the countries of Ammon, Moab, or Edom when they were traveling from Egypt to Canaan. So our ancestors went around those areas, and they did not destroy the people who lived there.
But now they are doing something bad to us, even though we were kind to them. They are trying to force us to leave the land that you gave to us as a place that would always belong to us!

Our God, please decide that they are wrong and defeat them. We ask you to do that because we are not able to defeat this huge army that is attacking us. We do not know what to do, but we are depending on you to help us.”
All the men of Judah were standing there with their wives, children, and babies in the presence of Yahweh {while Jehoshaphat prayed}.

In that great crowd there was a man whose name was Jahaziel. He was the son of Zechariah, the grandson of Benaiah, the great-grandson of Jeiel, and the great-great-grandson of Mattaniah. He was a Levite who was a descendant of Asaph. Yahweh’s Spirit inspired him,

and he said, “King Jehoshaphat and you people who live in Jerusalem and in other places throughout Judah, listen to me! This is what Yahweh says to you: ‘You will not have to fight against this huge army, because God will fight them and defeat them. So do not be afraid of them, and do not lose courage.
Tomorrow, march toward them. I can tell you that they will be coming up through the Ascent of Ziz. You will meet them at the end of the ravine near the wilderness of Jeruel.

But you will not need to fight a battle against them. The soldiers from Jerusalem and other places in Judah may form a battle line, but they should then stand still and watch what Yahweh does to save you. Do not be afraid and do not lose courage. March toward them tomorrow, and Yahweh will help you.’”
{When he heard this,} Jehoshaphat bowed down with his face touching the ground. All the people who were there from Jerusalem and other places in Judah bowed down in Yahweh’s presence to worship him.
Then some Levites who were descendants of Kohath and Korah stood up and very loudly praised Yahweh, the God of the Israelites.

Early the next morning, the army left to go to the desolate area near the town of Tekoa. As they were leaving, Jehoshaphat stood up and said to them, “You people from Jerusalem and other places in Judah, listen to me! Trust Yahweh our God! If you do that, you will be strong. Believe what he inspires people to say! If you do that, you will be successful.”

After discussing this with his military officers, Jehoshaphat had Levites march ahead of the soldiers. Those were Levites whose ministry was to sing to Yahweh and praise him for how wonderfully holy he is. They were singing, “Yahweh loves us faithfully forever, so praise him!”
The Ammonite, Moabite, and Edomite soldiers had been coming to attack Judah. But as soon as the Levites started to shout and praise Yahweh, Yahweh caused those soldiers to attack and kill each other.

What happened was that the Ammonite and Moabite soldiers first attacked the Edomite soldiers and completely destroyed them. After they had killed all of them, the Ammonitte and Moabite soldiers all killed each other.

When the Judeans came to the place where they could look out over the desolate area, they saw where that huge army was. But they saw that its soldiers lying dead on the ground! Not one of them was still alive.

So Jehoshaphat and his soldiers went to take the valuable possessions that had belonged to their enemies. They found much equipment and clothing and other valuable items. They collected these things until they could not carry any more. There were so many things that it took them three days to collect all of them.

The next day, they gathered in the Valley of Beracah. They praised Yahweh there, and that is why people called that place the Valley of Beracah{, which means “praise.”} People still call it that today.
Then Jehoshaphat led all the soldiers from Jerusalem and other places in Judah back home. Yahweh had enabled them to defeat their enemies, so they were very happy as they returned to Jerusalem.
When they arrived in Jerusalem, they went to the temple {to praise and thank Yahweh}. Levites and priests were playing lyres, harps, and trumpets.
The people of the kingdoms around Judah became very afraid of God when they learned how Yahweh had defeated the enemies of the Israelites.
After that, God kept the countries around him from attacking him, so Jehoshaphat’s kingdom was a peaceful place.

Jehoshaphat continued to rule Judah. He had been 35 years old when he started to rule, and he ruled in Jerusalem for 25 years. His mother was a woman whose name was Azubah. She was the daughter of Shilhi.
Throughout his life, Jehoshaphat lived as Yahweh wanted people to live, just as his father Asa had done.
However, he did not order his servants to destroy the shrines for worship on the top of hills. Most of the people were still not serious about obeying the God whom their ancestors had worshiped.

The accounts that Jehu son of Hanani wrote describe further things that Jehoshaphat did throughout his reign. Those accounts are in the book in which the kings of Israel recorded what happened during their reigns.
Later, Jehoshaphat, the king of Judah, made a peace treaty with Ahaziah, the king of Israel. That was a bad thing for Jehoshaphat to do.
They agreed to have their workers build a fleet of ships that were able to sail out on the sea. They built those ships at Ezion Geber.

But Eliezer son of Dodavahu from the city of Mareshah brought a message from God to Jehoshaphat. He told him, “Because you made a treaty with {that wicked king} Ahaziah, Yahweh is going to destroy what you have built.” Then there was a great storm at Ezion Geber that wrecked the ships, so they were never able to sail anywhere.
Then Jehoshaphat died. The Judeans buried him where they had buried his ancestors, in the part of Jerusalem that people called the City of David. His son Jehoram became the next king of Judah.
The Israelite king Jehoshaphat had several other sons who were Jehoram’s younger brothers. They were Azariah, Jehiel, Zechariah, Azariahu, Michael, and Shephatiah.

Their father had given them generous gifts of silver and gold and other valuable things. He also appointed them to rule various cities in Judah that had walls around them. But since Jehoram was his oldest son, he appointed him to be the king of Judah.

After Jehoram had become king and was completely in control of his father’s kingdom, he had his soldiers execute all of his younger brothers. He also had them execute some of the leaders of the nation.
Jehoram was 32 years old when he became the king, and he ruled in Jerusalem for 8 years.
Because his wife was one of Ahab’s daughters, he did the same kind of evil things that the kings of Israel did who were from Ahab’s family. He did things that Yahweh considered to be evil.
However, because Yahweh had made a covenant with King David, he did want to not end his dynasty. After all, Yahweh had promised David that his descendants would always be kings.
Judah had controlled Edom, but during Jehoram’s reign, the Edomites rebelled. They appointed their own king.

So Jehoram went with his army commanders and all of his chariots {to try to reconquer Edom}. But the Edomite commanders surrounded them with their chariots. Jehoram had to make a surprise attack against them at night (in order to escape}.

Since that time, Judah has no longer controlled Edom. Then, around that same time, the people of the city of Libnah also rebelled against Judah. Those things happened because Jehoram stopped obeying Yahweh, the God whom his ancestors had worshiped.
Instead, he built hilltop shrines for worshiping idols throughout Judah. He led the people who lived in Jerusalem and in other places in Judah be unfaithful to Yahweh by worshiping other gods.

So the prophet Elijah sent a letter to him. In it, he said, “Yahweh is the God whom your ancestor King David worshiped. This is what he says to you: ‘Bad things are going to happen to you because you have not lived as the previous kings of Judah lived. They were your father Jehoshaphat and {your grandfather} Asa.

Instead, you have lived as the kings of Israel live. You have led the people who live in Jerusalem and other places in Judah to be unfaithful to Yahweh by worshiping other gods. That is what the kings from the family of Ahab have done. You have also killed your brothers. They were part of the royal family, and they were better men than you are.
As a result, I, Yahweh, am about to cause great harm to the people of your kingdom, including your wives and children. I will also destroy much of your property.
I am also going to make you very sick. You will have a disease in your intestines that will become steadily worse until it makes your intestines come out.’”
Then Yahweh influenced some of the Philistines and some of the Arabs who lived near the Cushites to attack Jehoram.

They invaded Judah and defeated its defenders. That enabled them to go to Jerusalem and take away many valuable things that they found in the king’s palace. They also took away Jehoshaphat’s sons and wives. His youngest son, Jehoahaz, was the only one of his sons whom they did not take away.
After those bad things happened, Yahweh caused Jehoram to have an intestinal disease that no one could cure.

As a result, he was in severe pain every day. This continued for two whole years. At the end of that time, the disease made his intestines come out, and he died. The people of Judah had made great bonfires to honor his ancestors when they died. But they did not make a bonfire for Jehoram.

Jehoram was 32 years old when he became the king, and he ruled in Jerusalem for 8 years. When he died, no one wished that he were still alive. The Judeans buried him in the part of Jerusalem that people called the city of David. But they did not bury him in the royal tombs.

The Philistines and Arabs who had invaded Judah had killed all of Jehoram’s older sons. So the people who lived in Jerusalem appointed his youngest son Ahaziah to be their next king. Then Ahaziah ruled Judah after his father King Jehoram.
Ahaziah was 42 years old when he became the king. He ruled in Jerusalem for one year. His mother was a woman whose name was Athaliah. She was the granddaughter of King Omri of Israel.
Ahaziah’s mother advised him what to do, but she told him to do bad things. So he behaved just as the kings of Israel did who were descendants of Ahab.
Ahab’s family also advised him what to do after his father died. As a result, he did many things that Yahweh had told the Israelites were wrong. Ultimately, this destroyed him.

King Jehoram of Israel, who was Ahab’s son, led his soldiers to fight against the army of King Hazael of Aram. Following the advice of Ahab’s family, Ahaziah led his soldiers to help Jehoram. The armies fought near the city of Ramoth Gilead. The Aramean soldiers wounded Jehoram in the battle there.

Because the Arameans had wounded him when he fought with Hazael their king, Jehoram went back to the city of Jezreel to recover from his wounds. King Ahaziah of Judah learned that he had gone there to recover. So he went to Jezreel to visit him.

God influenced Ahaziah to go to visit Joram so that he would die at Jezreel. When Ahaziah arrived there, he went with Jehoram to meet Jehu son of Nimshi. Yahweh had appointed him to kill the descendants of Ahab.

While Jehu and the men who were with him were killing Ahab’s descendants, they found the leaders of Judah and the sons of Ahaziah’s relatives who were officers in Ahaziah’s royal court. They killed them too.

Then Jehu ordered his soldiers to look for Ahaziah. They found Ahaziah hiding in the city of Samaria. They brought him to Jehu and executed him. But they felt that they ought to bury him because he was a descendant of Jehoshaphat, who tried hard to please Yahweh. So they did bury him. After that, there were no descendants of Ahaziah who were powerful enough to become the next king of Judah.
Instead, when Ahaziah’s mother Athaliah learned that Jehu had killed her son, she ordered soldiers to kill all the members of Ahaziah’s family who might become the next king.

But King Jehoram had a daughter whose name was Jehoshabeath. She was the half-sister of Ahaziah, and she was the wife of Jehoiada the high priest. She rescued Ahaziah’s very young son Joash. While soldiers were killing his other sons, she took him away and hid him and his nursemaid in a room in the palace where people kept bedding supplies. Because she hid him, Athaliah did not know where he was, so her soldiers did not kill him.
For the next six years, the priests hid Joash in God’s temple. He lived with Jehoiada and Jehoshabeath. Meanwhile, Athaliah ruled Judah.

But after those six years, Jehoiada courageously made an agreement {to make Josiah the king} with some officers who each commanded a hundred soldiers. They were Azariah son of Jeroham, Ishmael son of Jehohanan, Azariah son of Obed, Maaseiah son of Adaiah, and Elishaphat son of Zichri.
Those men went throughout Judah to get Levites who lived in various cities in Judah along with Israelite clan leaders. They brought them back to Jerusalem.

They gathered at God’s temple. Jehoiada told them, “Yahweh said that the descendants of David should be our kings. So his descendant Josiah should be our king.” The Levites and leaders made a solemn agreement to obey Josiah as their king.

Jehoiada then gave them these instructions: “Many priests and Levites will come on duty on the Sabbath day. When they do{, the priests and Levites who have been here at the temple should not leave.} Instead, divide yourselves into three groups. One group must guard the entrances to the temple area.

Another group must watch the royal palace. The last group must guard the gate that leads from the palace to the temple. All the other people who have come here will stay in the courtyards in front of the temple.

Do not allow anyone to enter the temple except the priests and the Levites who are serving there. Yahweh has set them apart for their work, so they may go inside. But everyone else must obey Yahweh’s command not to enter the temple.

The Levites are to arm themselves with their weapons and stand all around the king to protect him. They are to kill anyone who tries to get into the temple {to harm the king}. If the king goes anywhere, they are to go with him.”

The Levites and all the Judeans who had come to Jerusalem did exactly what Jehoiada the priest told them to do. Jehoiada had told the Levites who were going off duty to stay at the temple, so they did. So the Levite leaders each organized those who were about to start their work on the Sabbath day and those who were just finishing their work.
Some spears, shields and large shields that had belonged to King David were in the temple. Jehoiada distributed them to the officers who commanded a hundred soldiers {to give to their men}.

Jehoiada had the soldiers with those weapons form a line all across the front of the temple. They stood between the temple building and the altar in its courtyard. In that way, they provided complete protection for the king.

Then Jehoiada brought Joash, the son of the last king, out of the temple. He put a crown on his head, and he gave him a scroll that recorded Yahweh’s laws. Then he and his sons poured olive oil on Joash’s head {to show that he was now the king}. The people shouted, “May King Joash rule for a long time!”
Athaliah heard the noise that the people were making as they ran over to Joash and as they shouted to praise him. So she came to the temple where the people had gathered.

She saw Joash, the new king, standing next to one of the big pillars on the temple porch. She saw military commanders and musicians playing trumpets standing next to him. She heard a crowd of ordinary Israelites shouting joyfully. The priests were blowing trumpets, and the Levites were singing and playing musical instruments to lead the people in worship. She tore her clothes {to show her distress} and shouted, “You are traitors! You have betrayed me!”

Jehoiada told the officers who commanded a hundred soldiers, whom he had put in charge of the armed men that day, “Have the guards take her away from the temple. Kill anyone who tries to rescue her!” He said that because he did not want his men to kill her near Yahweh’s temple.

The guards formed two lines so that she could walk safely between them {back to the palace}. She walked through the entrance that horses used to get into the palace courtyard. The guards killed her there.
Then Jehoiada had the people make a solemn agreement with him and with the king that they would always be loyal to Yahweh as their God.

Then the large crowd of Israelites who had gathered went to the temple of Baal. They destroyed the main altar, smashed the statues of Baal into pieces, and tore down the temple building. They also killed Mattan, the priest of Baal, right in front of the other altars in the temple.

Then Jehoiada organized the priests to resume their duties at the temple. They were to offer sacrifices to Yahweh that they burned completely on the altar, as Moses had said in the law that they should do. He also organized the Levites to resume their duties. David had said that they should perform joyful music at the temple, and he had assigned various responsibilities to different groups of Levites.
Jehoiada also had the Levite gatekeepers resume their duties of guarding the gates of the temple courtyard. They were to make sure that only people who were ritually clean entered the courtyard.

Then Jehoiada gathered the officers who commanded a hundred soldiers, the Judean nobles, other Judean leaders, and all the people who had come from throughout Judea. They brought the king from the temple to the palace. Joash entered the palace through its Upper Gate. The people had him sit down on the same throne where the previous kings of Judah had sat.
People throughout Judah were glad that the guards had executed Athaliah. The city of Jerusalem became a peaceful place after she died.
Joash was seven years old when he became the king of Judah, and he ruled in Jerusalem for 40 years. His mother was a woman whose name was Zibiah. She was from the city of Beersheba.
Joash did what Yahweh considered to be right for as long as Jehoiada was the high priest.
Jehoiada arranged for Joash to marry two wives. He had sons and daughters with them.
Later, Joash wanted to repair the temple.

He summoned the priests and Levites and told them, “Go throughout Judah and collect from the people the money that the law of Moses requires them to pay each year. Then use that money to pay for repairing the temple. Do that immediately.” But the Levites did not do that immediately.

So the king summoned Jehoiada, the high priest. He told him, “Yahweh’s servant Moses required the Israelites to pay a tax to care for the sacred tent. You should have required the Levites to collect that tax from the people who live in Jerusalem and other places in Judah {so that we could repair the temple}.”
The temple needed repairs because the sons of that wicked woman Athaliah had broken into it. They had also taken the special items that were in it and used them to worship Baal.
King Joash commanded Jehoiada to make a chest and put it just outside the entrance to the temple courtyard.

Then the king sent messengers to tell the people who lived in Jerusalem and other places in Judah to bring their tax money to the temple. That is what God’s servant Moses had required the Israelites to do when they were in the desolate area between Egypt and Canaan.
All of the Judean leaders and other people agreed, and they gladly brought their contributions. They put their money into the chest and filled it up.

From time to time, the Levites would see that there was a lot of money in the chest. When that happened, they would carry the chest to the officials whom the king had put in charge of the temple restoration. The king’s secretary and the assistant to the high priest would come and take the money out of the chest. Then the Levites would carry the chest back and put it outside the courtyard entrance again. They did this regularly, and they collected a great amount of money.

The king and Jehoiada paid the money to the men who were supervising the work of repairing the temple. Those men hired stoneworkers and carpenters to repair the temple. They also hired metalworkers to make items of iron and bronze to restore the temple.

The men who were making the repairs worked hard, and through their efforts they put the temple in good condition again. They restored the temple according to its original design, and they made it stronger.

There was still money left when they had finished the repair work. So they brought that money to the king and to Jehoiada. They told the workers to use that money to make items for the priests to use in the temple. So they made tools for the priests to use when offering sacrifices that that they burned completely on the altar. They also made dishes and other gold and silver items for the temple. For long as Jehoiada lived, the priests offered sacrifices at the temple each morning and evening that they burned completely on the altar.
Jehoiada lived for a long time. He was 130 years old when he died.

The Judeans buried him in the part of Jerusalem that people called the City of David. That is where they buried their kings. They buried him there because he had done good things for the Israelites and for God and his temple.
But after Jehoiada died, the Judean leaders came to Joash and bowed down low in front of him {to flatter him}. Then they persuaded him to do what they wanted.

The Judeans stopped worshiping Yahweh, the God whom their ancestors had worshiped, at his temple. Instead, they worshiped Asherah and other false gods. Yahweh became very angry with the people who lived in Jerusalem and other places in Judah for sinning in this way.
Yahweh sent prophets to tell them to worship him again. The prophets showed the people that they were wrong to worship other gods. But the people did not do what the prophets told them to do.

Then God’s Spirit inspired Zechariah, who was the son of Jehoiada the high priest. He stood up {n the inner courtyard of the temple} above the people {who were in the outer courtyard}. He told them, “This is what God says, ‘You must not disobey the commandments that I, Yahweh, have given you! You will not succeed if you do that. Because you no longer worship me, Yahweh, I will no longer protect you.”
But the leaders of Judah made a secret plan against Zechariah. King Joash ordered them to kill him. So they killed him by throwing stones at him in the temple courtyard.

Zechariah’s father Jehoiada had always helped King Joash, but he was not grateful for that. Instead, he commanded people to kill Jehoiada’s son. That son, Zechariah, said as he was dying, “I hope that Yahweh will recognize what a wicked thing these people have done and punish them for doing it!”

In the spring of the following year, the army of Aram attacked Joash’s kingdom. They invaded Judah and conquered Jerusalem. They killed all of the Judean leaders. They took many valuable possessions and sent them back to their king, who ruled in the city of Damascus.

The Aramean army that invaded Judah did not have very many soldiers. The Judean army was much larger. But Yahweh allowed the Arameans to defeat the Judeans. Yahweh did that to punish Joash because he had led the Judeans to stop worshiping him, the God whom their ancestors had worshiped.

The Arameans severely wounded Joash when he fought against them. So after the Arameans left, some of his officials made a secret plan against him because he had killed Zechariah and the other sons of Jehoiada the high priest. They killed him while he was lying in bed trying to recover from his wounds. When Joash died, the Judeans buried him in the part of Jerusalem that people called the City of David. But they did not bury him in the royal tombs.
One of the officials who made a secret plan against Joash was Zabad. His mother Shimeath was an Ammonitess. The other official was Jehozabad. His mother Shimrith was a Moabitess.

There is an account of Joash’s reign in the book in which the kings of Judah and Israel recorded what happened during their reigns. This account describes Joash’s sons and what they did. It also records the many oracles that prophets spoke against him. It also describes what he did to repair the temple. After Joash died, his son Amaziah became the next king.
Amaziah was 25 years old when he became the king of Judah, and he ruled in Jerusalem for 29 years. His mother’s name was Jehoaddan. She was from Jerusalem.
Amaziah did what Yahweh considered to be right, but not wholeheartedly.
As soon as he completely controlled his kingdom, he had his soldiers execute the officials who had murdered his father, King Joash.

But he did not order his soldiers to execute their sons. He obeyed what Moses wrote in the book of the law. Yahweh had commanded, “You must not execute parents for what their children do, and you must not execute children for what their parents do. Execute people only for the sins that they themselves commit.”

Amaziah ordered the men in his kingdom to come to Jerusalem. He organized the men of the tribes of Judah and Benjamin by clans into military units. He appointed officers to command groups of a thousand soldiers and of a hundred soldiers. They counted the men who were at least 20 years old, and they found that there were 300,000 men who were capable soldiers who could fight well with spears and shields.
Amaziah also hired 100,000 capable soldiers from Israel. He paid almost 3,300 kilograms of silver to hire them.

But a prophet came to him and told him, “Your Majesty, Yahweh does not help any soldiers from the northern kingdom of Israel. So you must not allow those soldiers from Israel to march with your soldiers.

God is able to help an army win a battle or to make an army lose a battle. So you and your own soldiers must be courageous and go and fight. {If you rely on soldiers from Israel,} God will allow your enemies to defeat you.
Amaziah told that prophet, “If those soldiers do not help us, then I will get nothing for the 3,300 kilograms of silver that I paid to hire them!”
So Amaziah removed the Israelite soldiers from his army and told them to go back home. This made them very angry with the Judeans. As they started to march back home, they were still very angry.
Amaziah felt brave enough to lead an army of only his own soldiers. They fought against the Edomites in the Valley of Salt and killed 10,000 of them.
The Judeans also captured 10,000 other soldiers. They took them to the top of a cliff and threw them down over the cliff. Their bodies broke apart when they hit the ground{, and they all died}.

Meanwhile, the soldiers whom Amaziah had hired but then not allowed to fight with him attacked cities in Judah. They had come from the city of Samaria {in Israel}, and they attacked cities as far into Judah {from there} as Beth Horon. They killed 3,000 people and took away many valuable things.

Amaziah returned to Jerusalem after his army had defeated the Edomites. He had captured some idols that represented the gods that people worshiped in Edom. He made a shrine for them as his own gods. Then he bowed down to worship them, and he offered sacrifices to them.

This made Yahweh very angry with Amaziah. He sent a prophet to him, who told him, “It does not make sense for you to worship these gods! When your army attacked the people who worshiped them, they were not able to protect them!”
But while he was still speaking, the king told him, “You are not one of my advisors. So stop talking! Otherwise, I will have my soldiers execute you!”

Then King Amaziah of Judah, after consulting his advisors, sent messengers to King Joash of Israel. Joash was the son of Jehoahaz and the grandson of Jehu. The messengers said on behalf of Amaziah, “I challenge you to a battle!”

But in response, King Joash sent messengers to tell King Amaziah a story that taught a lesson. They said, “Once a little thornbush was growing in the mountains in Lebanon. It sent a message to a great cedar tree. It told the cedar that it should allow the son of the thornbush to marry its daughter. But as a wild animal in Lebanon was walking along, it stepped on the thornbush and crushed it.

You are thinking, ‘I have defeated the Edomites{, so I must have a powerful army}!’ You have become proud and boastful. But you should stay home. If you cause trouble by fighting against me, I will defeat you and harm you and your kingdom.”
But Amaziah did not withdraw his challenge. That happened because God wanted Joash’s army to defeat his army because he was worshiping the gods of Edom.
So King Joash of Israel led his army to fight against the army of King Amaziah of Judah. They fought a battle at the city of Beth Shemesh in Judah.
The Israelite army defeated the army of Judah, and the Judean soldiers ran away and went home.

The soldiers of King Joash of Israel captured King Amaziah of Judah at Beth Shemesh. Amaziah was the son of Joash and the grandson of Ahaziah. King Joash brought Amaziah back to Jerusalem {as a prisoner}. His soldiers tore down the wall around the city from the Ephraim Gate to the Corner Gate. That section of the wall was about 180 meters long.

His soldiers seized all the gold and silver and valuable items that were in God’s temple that the descendants of Obed Edom were guarding. They also took the valuable things that Amaziah was keeping in his royal palace. They also took some prisoners to make sure that Amaziah would not attack Israel. Then King Joash returned to Samaria.
Later, Joash son of Jehoahaz, the king of Israel, died. Amaziah son of Joash, the king of Judah, lived for 15 years after that.
The book in which the kings of Judah and Israel recorded what happened during their reigns describes further things that Amaziah did throughout his reign.

As soon as Amaziah started to worship other gods instead of Yahweh, some men in Jerusalem made a secret plan to kill him. {When they tried to do that,} he ran away to the city of Lachish. But those people sent men to follow him to Lachish, and those men killed him there.

{To honor him,} his officials brought his body back to Jerusalem in his own chariot. They buried him in the part of Jerusalem that people called the City of David. That was where people had also buried his ancestors.
Then the Judeans appointed Amaziah’s son Uzziah as the next king. He became king when he was 16 years old.
After his father Amaziah died, Uzziah led his army to recapture the city of Eloth. He then fortified that city.
Uzziah was 16 years old when he started to rule, and he ruled in Jerusalem for 52 years. His mother’s name was Jecoliah. She was from the city of Jerusalem.
He did things that Yahweh considered to be right. He did the same good things that his father Amaziah had done.
A man whose name was Zechariah taught Uzziah to honor God. For as long as Zechariah was alive, he obeyed God. While Uzziah obeyed Yahweh, God made him successful.

Uzziah led his army to fight against the Philistines. They {conquered} the cities of Gath, Jabneh, and Ashdod and tore down their walls. Then he built forts near Ashdod and in other places in Philistia.
God helped Uzziah and his army to defeat the armies of the Philistines, the Arabs who lived in the city of Gur Baal, and the Meunites.
The Ammonites sent tribute to Uzziah each year. Uzziah became so powerful that even the Egyptians knew that he was a great king.
Uzziah had his workers build defensive towers in Jerusalem at the Corner Gate, the Valley Gate, and the place where the wall bends {defensively}. They built very strong towers.

Uzziah owned large herds of cattle. They grazed in the foothills of Judah and in the plains. So Uzziah also had his workers build towers in those areas and dig out many cisterns. Uzziah was very interested in farming, so he had his servants farm the land and care for his vineyards in the hills and in the fertile areas.

Uzziah had an army of soldiers who fought well. They were in groups that were ready to go out and fight. Jeiel, the king’s secretary, and Maaseiah, one of the army officers, counted the men and placed them in groups. Hananiah, one of the king’s officials, supervised them.
Their clan leaders led these capable soldiers into battle. There were 2,600 of those leaders.
The groups that those leaders commanded made up an army of 307,500 soldiers who fought well. It was a very powerful army, ready to fight the king’s enemies.
Uzziah supplied the entire army with shields, spears, helmets, armor, bows and arrows, and slings for throwing stones.

In Jerusalem, his skilled workers made catapults to put on the towers and on the corners of the walls. Those catapults could hurl large stones and launch huge arrows. God helped Uzziah in special ways {as he did these things} so that he became very powerful. As a result, Uzziah became famous even in places that were far from Judah.

But when Uzziah became powerful, he became proud, and he did something that was very wrong. He disobeyed Yahweh his God by going inside his temple to burn incense on the altar where only priests could burn incense.
Azariah, the high priest, and 80 other brave priests followed him into the temple.

They tried to stop him. They told him, “Uzziah, you do not have the right to burn incense to Yahweh {on this altar}! Only the priests, the descendants of Aaron, whom Yahweh set apart, have the right to do that. You have disobeyed Yahweh our God, and he will disgrace you for doing that! So you must leave the temple immediately!”

Uzziah became furious with the priests. He was holding a censer and had been just about to burn some incense. He yelled at the priests, and as he did, leprosy appeared on his forehead, right there in the temple next to the incense altar where the priests had confronted him.

Azariah the high priest and the other priests looked at him and saw that he had leprosy on his forehead. They made him leave the temple right away. Uzziah himself hurried to leave the temple when he realized that Yahweh had punished him in this way.

King Uzziah remained a leper for the rest of his life. So he had to live in a house away from other people, and he could not enter the courtyard of the temple. His son Jotham was in charge of the royal palace and decided cases that Judeans brought to him.
The prophet Isaiah son of Amoz wrote an account of further things that Uzziah did throughout his entire reign.

When Uzziah died, because he had been a leper, the Judeans did not bury him in the royal tombs. Instead, they buried him in a nearby cemetery that the kings owned. His son Jotham became the next king of Judah.
Jotham was 25 years old when he became the king of Judah. He ruled from Jerusalem for 16 years. His mother’s name was Jerushah. She was the daughter of Zadok.

Jotham did things that Yahweh considered to be right. He did the same things that his father Uzziah had done, except that he did not go into Yahweh’s temple {to burn incense as his father had tried to do}. Nevertheless, the people of Judah continued to worship idols.
Jotham had his workers rebuild the Upper Gate of the temple. They also did much to repair the wall on the hill of Ophel.
He also had them build cities in the hills of Judah and forts and towers in the forests.

He led his army to fight against the Ammonite king and his army, and his soldiers defeated them. He made them to pay a tribute of about three and one-third metric tons of silver, 2,200 kiloliters of wheat, and 2,200 kiloliters of barley. They paid it that year and for each of the next two years.
Jotham faithfully obeyed Yahweh his God, and as a result, he became a powerful king.
The book in which the kings of Israel and Judah recorded what happened during their reigns describes further things that Jotham did, including the battles that he fought and how he lived.
Jotham had been 25 years old when he became king, and he ruled from Jerusalem for 16 years.
Then he died, and the Judeans buried him in the part of Jerusalem that people called the City of David. His son Ahaz became the next king.
Ahaz was 20 years old when he became the king of Judah. He ruled from Jerusalem for 16 years. He did not do things that Yahweh considered to be right, as his ancestor David had done.
Instead, he lived in the sinful way that the kings of Israel lived. He even had his workers make metal images of the god Baal {that he worshiped as idols}.

He burned incense {to false gods} in the Valley of Ben Hinnom. He even burned his own sons as sacrifices to false gods. He did the same disgusting things as the people whom Yahweh forced to leave the land of Canaan so that the Israelites could live there.
He offered sacrifices and burned incense {to idols} at shrines, on hilltops, and under many big trees.

As a result, Yahweh, the God he should have worshiped, allowed the army of the king of Aram to defeat his army. The Aramean army won a great victory over him and captured many Judean soldiers and took them as prisoners to Damascus. Yahweh also allowed the army of the king of Israel to defeat the army of Judah. The Israelite soldiers killed very many of the Judean soldiers.

In one day, the {Israelite} army of Pekah son of Remaliah killed 120,000 capable Judean soldiers. That happened because the people of Judah had abandoned Yahweh, the God whom their ancestors had worshiped.
Zichri, a great soldier from the tribe of Ephraim, killed King Ahaz’s son Maaseiah. He also killed Azrikam, who was in charge of the palace, and Elkanah, the king’s most important official.

The Israelite soldiers captured 200,000 Judeans, who were their kinsmen. This included many of the wives, sons, and daughters of the Judean soldiers. The Israelites also took many valuable possessions from them and brought them back to Samaria.

But a prophet of Yahweh whose name was Oded lived in Samaria. He went out of the city to meet the soldiers as they were returning. He told them, “Pay attention! Yahweh, the God whom your ancestors worshiped, was angry with the people of Judah. That is why he allowed you to defeat them. But you killed them in a very cruel way. God in heaven saw what you did.

And now you want {to do a further bad thing} by making men and women from Jerusalem and other places in Judah your slaves. But consider that you have already done many things to offend Yahweh, the God whom you should worship.
Now listen to me! Yahweh is extremely angry with you for taking your own kinsmen as prisoners. So you must allow them to return home.”

Then some of the leaders of the tribe of Ephraim rebuked the soldiers who were returning from the battle. Those leaders were Azariah son of Johanan, Berekiah son of Meshillemoth, Jehizkiah son of Shallum, and Amasa son of Hadlai.

They told the soldiers, “We are guilty of committing many sins against Yahweh. Yahweh is already very angry with us Israelites. So what you are doing will make Yahweh consider us even more guilty for the sins we have committed. So you must not bring those prisoners here!”
So while their leaders and the people of Samaria watched, the soldiers released the prisoners. They also returned to them the valuable possessions that they had taken.

The leaders assigned some men to care for the prisoners. These men took some of the clothes that the soldiers had taken from the people of Judah and gave those clothes to any of the people who lacked clothing. They also gave sandals to prisoners who did not have any. They made sure that they all had enough to eat and drink, and they gave them olive oil to rub on their wounds. They provided donkeys for anyone to ride who was too weak to walk. Then they brought them all to Jericho, which was on the border of Judah. (People also call Jericho the City of Palms.) Then the Israelites who had been helping the prisoners returned to Samaria.
About that time, King Ahaz sent a message to the king of Assyria asking him to help him.
The Edomite army had also come and attacked Judah and taken away many people as prisoners.

Philistine soldiers had also raided cities in the foothills and in the southern Judean wilderness. They had captured the cities of Beth Shemesh, Aijalon, and Gederoth. They had also captured Soko, Timnah, and Gimzo and the surrounding villages. Philistines settled in those places.

King Ahaz had encouraged the people of Judah to do wicked things, and he had disobeyed Yahweh greatly. So those things happened because Yahweh was punishing the Judeans for what Ahaz had led them to do.
Tilgath Pilneser, the king of Assyria, led his army to that area. But instead of helping Ahaz, he caused trouble for him.
Ahaz took some valuable things from Yahweh’s temple and from his royal palace and from the leaders of Judah. He sent them to the Assyrian king. But this only made Ahaz poorer
While he was experiencing those troubles, King Ahaz disobeyed Yahweh even more.

The army of the Aramean kingdom of Damascus had defeated the army of Ahaz. Ahaz thought, “The gods that the Aramean kings worship are helping them. So I will worship those gods, and then they will help me too.” So Ahaz offered sacrifices to those gods. But worshiping those gods caused great trouble for Ahaz and his whole kingdom.

Ahaz collected the items that the priests used in God’s temple and cut them into pieces. He locked the doors of Yahweh’s temple and set up his own altars {for worshiping idols} at street corners throughout Jerusalem.

He had his workers build hilltop shrines in cities throughout Judah. People offered sacrifices to other gods at those shrines. By doing this, Ahaz made Yahweh, the God whom his ancestors had worshiped, very angry.
The book in which the kings of Judah and Israel recorded what happened during their reigns describes further things that Ahaz did and how he lived throughout his reign.
When Ahaz died, the Judeans buried him within the city of Jerusalem. But they did not bury him in the royal tombs. His son Hezekiah became the next king.
Hezekiah was 25 years old when he became the king of Judah. He ruled from Jerusalem for 29 years. His mother’s name was Abijah. She was the daughter of Zechariah.
Hezekiah did things that Yahweh considered to be right, just as his ancestor King David had done.
During the first year that Hezekiah was ruling Judah, in the first month of the year, he unlocked the doors of the temple. He had his workers repair them.
Then he gathered the priests and Levites in the courtyard on the east side of the temple.

He told them, “Listen to me, all you descendants of Levi! I want you to remove from the temple area everything that people have been using to worship idols. To do that, first wash yourselves to become ritually clean. Then you will be able to make Yahweh’s temple a place that is once again set apart for him, the God whom your ancestors worshiped.

You must cleanse the temple because our ancestors disobeyed God. They did many things that Yahweh, our God, considered to be evil. They worshiped other gods instead of him. {When they offered sacrifices,} they no longer faced the Most Holy Place where Yahweh is present in a special way. Instead, they turned their backs to that place.

They also locked the doors of the temple, and they no longer kept the lamps burning all night. They did not burn any incense to honor Yahweh, the God of us Israelites. They did not offer sacrifices to him {each morning and evening} that the priests burned completely on the altar in temple courtyard.

This made Yahweh very angry with the people who live in Jerusalem and other places in Judah. This has made the people of other nations very frightened that they will become like us. They hiss at us {in contempt}. You have experienced this personally.
That is why our enemies were able to kill our ancestors in battle. That is why they were able to capture our sons and daughters and wives and take them away to other countries.
But now I intend to make a covenant with Yahweh, the God of us Israelites, so that he will no longer be angry with us.
You who are like my sons, Yahweh has chosen you to stand in his presence as his servants. He has chosen you to serve him by offering sacrifices. So fulfill that responsibility once again right away.”

Several leaders of the Levites responded to what King Hezekiah had said. They included Mahath son of Amasai and Joel son of Azariah from the descendants of Kohath. From the descendants of Merari, there were Kish son of Abdi and Azariah son of Jehallelel. From the descendants of Gershon, there were Joah son of Zimmah and Eden son of Joah.
From the descendants of Elizaphan, there were Shimri and Jeiel. From the descendants of Asaph, there were Zechariah and Mattaniah.
From the descendants of Heman, there were Jehiel and Shimei. From the descendants of Jeduthun, there were Shemaiah and Uzziel.

Those men gathered their fellow Levites, and they all washed themselves to become ritually clean. Then they went to the temple area to remove everything that people had been using to worship idols. They worked to restore the arrangements for worship that Yahweh had described in the law of Moses. That is what the king had commanded them to do.

The priests went into the temple building to make it a holy place again. They brought out to the temple courtyard everything that they found inside the temple that people had been using to worship idols. Then the Levites took those things out of the city down to the Kidron Valley {and burned them there}.

The priests and Levites began this work on the first day of the first month of the year. It took them eight days to clear out the temple courtyard. It took them another eight days to clear out the temple building. But by the sixteenth day of that month, they had finished making Yahweh’s temple once again a special place for him.

Representatives of the priests and Levites went to the royal palace to speak with King Hezekiah.. They told him, “We have now removed everything idolatrous from everywhere in the temple area. This includes the altar on which the priests completely burn sacrifices and all the tools that the priests use to do that. It also includes the table on which the priests display fresh bread before Yahweh each week and all the tools that the priests use to do that.

When Ahaz was our king, he disobeyed God, and he discarded all the items that the priests used in the temple area. But we have {found and} repaired those items, and we have dedicated them for the priests to use again. We have put them back in front of Yahweh’s altar.”
Early the next morning, King Hezekiah gathered the city officials together. They all went to the courtyard of the temple.

They brought with them seven bulls, seven rams, and seven male lambs. They also brought seven male goats. Those goats would be an offering to ask Yahweh to forgive the sins that the king and the people of Judah had committed. This offering was also to ask Yahweh to accept the temple once again as a place where people would worship him. The king commanded the {legitimate} priests, who were descendants of Aaron, to offer those animals as sacrifices to Yahweh on the altar.

So first the city officials slaughtered the bulls, and the priests took the blood from them and sprinkled it on the altar. Then the officials slaughtered the rams, and the priests sprinkled their blood on the altar. Then the officials slaughtered the lambs, and the priests sprinkled their blood on the altar.

The goats were to be an offering to ask Yahweh to forgive the sins of the Judeans. Someone led the goats in front of the king and the people who had gathered in the temple courtyard. The king and the people laid their hands on those goats.

Then the priests slaughtered the goats and sprinkled their blood on the altar. They did that as an offering to ask Yahweh to forgive the sins that all the Israelites had committed. They did that because the king had told them to burn the animals completely on the altar and make this sin offering on behalf of all the people of Israel.

The king had told the Levites to stand in the temple courtyard with cymbals, lyres, and harps. That was what King David and his prophets Gad and Nathan had commanded. They gave this commandment by Yahweh’s authority, in obedience to the messages that he had given to his prophets.
So some Levites were standing in the temple courtyard with the musical instruments that King David had provided. The priests had trumpets.

Then Hezekiah told the priests to burn the animals completely on the altar. As soon as they started to do that, those Levites began to play the instruments that David had provided when he was the king of Israel. Some other Levites started to sing to praise Yahweh, and the priests played their trumpets, following the tune that those Levites were playing on their instruments.

While the Levites sang and the priests played their trumpets, people throughout the crowd kept bowing down to worship Yahweh. They continued to do that until the priests had finished burning all the animals completely on the altar.
When they finished burning all the animals, the king and all the city officials knelt down and worshiped Yahweh.

Then King Hezekiah and the city officials told the Levites to praise Yahweh by singing songs that David and the prophet Asaph had composed. So the Levites sang those songs, and they and the people became joyful, and the people bowed down and worshiped Yahweh.

Then Hezekiah said to everyone who was present, “You have now dedicated yourselves to worship only Yahweh. So bring forward to the temple courtyard animals to provide meat for feasts to thank Yahweh for what he has done for you.” So the people brought forward animals to sacrifice for meals to thank Yahweh. Some who wished also brought animals for the priests to burn completely on the altar.
Altogether the people brought 70 bulls, 100 rams, and 200 male lambs for the priests to burn completely on the altar as sacrifices to Yahweh.
The people brought 600 bulls and 3,000 sheep to provide meat for feasts to thank Yahweh.

It was the duty of the priests to remove the skins from the animals that they burned completely on the altar. However, the Levites had been more eager to make themselves ritually clean than the priests had been. As a result, there were not enough priests available to skin all the animals that the people offered. So the Levites, their kinsmen, helped them complete this work. They continued to help them until enough priests had made themselves ritually clean.

The Levites also helped the priests skin the animals because there were so many of them to burn completely on the altar. The priests also had to prepare offerings of wine to accompany the sacrifice of each of those animals. They also had to burn on the altar the fat from the animals that provided the meat for the feasts.
Because they had been able to restore the worship at the temple so quickly, Hezekiah and the people of Judah recognized that God had enabled them to do this, and this made them very happy.

King Hezekiah wanted people throughout the kingdoms of Israel and Judah to come and celebrate the Passover festival at the temple in Jerusalem to honor Yahweh their God. He would send messengers to invite them, and he would write a special letter to the people of the northern kingdom of Israel. However, not enough of the priests had yet made themselves ritually clean, and it would take time for people to travel to Jerusalem. So they could not celebrate the festival during the first month of the year {as the law specified}. Instead, the king and his officials and the people of Jerusalem decided to celebrate Passover the following month.
The king and the people agreed that this was a good plan.

So they resolved to send messengers throughout the land of Israel, from Beersheba {in the far south} to Dan {in the far north}. Those messengers invited people to come to Jerusalem to celebrate the Passover to honor Yahweh their God. They sent the messengers because previously people from throughout Israel had not come to celebrate Passover, even though Moses wrote in the law that they should.

Obeying the king’s command, messengers went throughout Israel and Judah. They brought letters that the king and his officials had written. The letters said, “Yahweh is the God whom {your ancestors} Abraham, Isaac, and Israel worshiped. The kings of Assyria have taken away many of your people, but the rest of you are still living in your land. If you Israelites become loyal to Yahweh again, he will protect you.

Do not be like your ancestors and your kinsmen, who worshiped gods other than Yahweh, the God whom their ancestors had worshiped. You know that as a result, Yahweh punished them so severely that other people are now afraid of becoming like them.

So do not be stubborn as your ancestors were. Pledge your loyalty to Yahweh again. Come to his temple, which he has set apart for his honor forever, to worship Yahweh your God. If you do that, he will no longer be angry with you.

Indeed, if you are loyal to Yahweh again, the enemies who took away your kinsmen and your children will act kindly toward them. They will allow them to return to this land. This will happen because Yahweh your God is kind and merciful. If you become loyal to him again, he will treat you favorably.”

The messengers went to cities throughout the northern kingdom of Israel as far north as the territory of the tribe of Zebulun. However, most of the people they spoke to laughed at them and ridiculed them.
However, some people from the tribes of Asher, Manasseh, and Zebulun were sorry for their sins, and they came to Jerusalem.
And God influenced the people of Judah to make them willing together to obey the command of the king and his officials and do what Yahweh’s law required.
As a result, many people gathered in Jerusalem in the second month of the year to celebrate the Festival of Unleavened Bread. They were a very large crowd of people.

First, they removed the altars that were in Jerusalem {for offering sacrifices} to false gods. They also removed all the altars for burning incense to false gods. They burned those altars in the Kidron Valley.

Then they killed the Passover lambs, on the fourteenth day of the second month. The priests and Levites who had not yet washed themselves to become ritually clean felt shame. They did wash themselves, and they brought animals to the temple {as sacrifices for their sins} that the priests burned completely on the altar.

Moses, that special servant of God, had written in the law where the priests should stand. The priests stood in those places. The Levites handed them bowls containing the blood {from lambs they had killed}, and the priests sprinkled that blood on the altar.

The Levites had killed those lambs because many people in the crowd had not become ritually clean, so they could not kill the lambs themselves as sacrifices to Yahweh {as the law directed}. As a result, the Levites were responsible for killing the Passover lambs for them.

In fact, many of the people had not become ritually clean. Many of them had come from the tribes of Ephraim, Manasseh, Issachar, and Zebulun. But they ate the Passover meal anyway, even though Moses had written in the law that people had to be clean to eat it. But Hezekiah prayed for those people. He prayed, “Yahweh, you always do what is right. I ask you to forgive
everyone who sincerely wants to honor you, Yahweh, the God whom his ancestors worshiped. Please do that even if they have not purified themselves as they should in order to worship at your temple.”
Yahweh agreed to do what Hezekiah asked, and he did not punish the people.

The Israelites who had come to Jerusalem celebrated the Festival of Unleavened Bread very happily for seven days. The priests and Levites sang to praise Yahweh each day and played loud musical instruments that belonged to Yahweh’s temple.

Hezekiah thanked all those Levites for devoting themselves to Yahweh and leading the people in worship so skillfully. For those seven days, the people celebrated the Passover festival. They sacrificed fellowship offerings and thanked Yahweh, the God whom their ancestors had worshiped.
Then the people who had gathered in Jerusalem agreed to celebrate for seven more days. So they celebrated joyfully for seven more days.

So that they could do that, King Hezekiah provided 1,000 bulls and 7,000 sheep for the people to eat during the festival. The leaders also provided 1,000 bulls and 10,000 sheep for the people to eat. Many priests made themselves ritually clean {so that they could serve at this festival}.

The people who had gathered from other places in Judah were very happy. So were the priests and Levites. So were the people who had come to Jerusalem from the northern kingdom of Israel. So were the foreigners who lived in that kingdom or in Judah who had come for the festival.
There had not been a celebration like this one in Jerusalem since the time when David’s son Solomon was the king of Israel. So the people at the festival were very happy.

{At the end of the festival,} the {legitimate} priests, who were descendants of Levi, stood up and asked God to make good things happen for the people. In heaven, the holy place where he lives, God heard their prayer, and he did what they asked.

After the festival ended, the Israelites who had come to Jerusalem went out to the other cities in Judah. They smashed the stone pillars that people had set up to honor false gods. They cut down the wooden images that represented the goddess Asherah. They destroyed the altars and hilltop shrines for worshiping foreign gods. They did that throughout the territory of the tribe of Judah, and also throughout the territories of Benjamin, Ephraim, and Manasseh, until none remained. Then all of those Israelites each returned to their own homes in the cities and towns where they lived.

Hezekiah organized the priests and Levites back into groups. He had each group do the work that King David had originally assigned to it. The priests would once again burn sacrifices completely on the altar and sacrifice fellowship offerings. The Levites would once again help them and also sing and play instruments to thank and praise Yahweh in the temple courtyard.

King Hezekiah contributed sheep from his own flocks for the sacrifices that the priests would burn completely on the altar. The priests offered those sacrifices in the morning and in the evening each day. They also offered them on Sabbath days, on New Moon festivals, and at each of the feasts that the Israelites celebrated each year. Moses had written in Yahweh’s law that they should do that.

Hezekiah commanded the people who lived in Jerusalem to bring the priests and Levites the part of their crops that belonged to them. That would allow them to do the work that Yahweh’s law had assigned to them.

As soon as the Israelites heard this command, they generously contributed the first grain that they harvested and the first wine and olive oil that they produced. They also contributed honey as they acquired it. They later contributed a tenth of all the crops that had grown in their fields. When they brought this to the temple, it was a very large amount.

The people of the tribe of Judah and other Israelite tribes who were living in various cities in Judah also brought a tenth of the animals in their herds and flocks. They also contributed animals that they had set apart for Yahweh their God as freewill offerings or to pay vows. The people gave so much that they made huge piles.

They began to bring their contributions in the third month of the year{, when they celebrated the start of the harvest}. They kept contributing until the seventh month{, when they celebrated the end of the harvest}.
When Hezekiah and his officials came and saw the huge piles, they praised Yahweh and asked him to make good things happen for the people who had given these gifts.
Then Hezekiah asked the priests and Levites how they had so much food that piles of it remained.

Azariah the high priest, a descendant of Zadok, replied, “Since the time that the people started to bring their offerings to the temple, we have been able to eat all that we need and still have plenty remaining. This has happened because Yahweh has enabled his people to grow many crops. As a result, this great amount of food remains.
So Hezekiah told them to arrange to keep these supplies in storerooms at the temple. So they arranged to do that.

Then they put in those storerooms the people’s contributions of the first grain they had harvested, the tenth of their crops, and the animals that people had set apart to give to Yahweh. They did this honestly. A Levite whose name was Conaniah was in charge of these supplies. His younger brother Shimei was his assistant.

{The high priest} Azariah was in charge of everything at the temple. He and King Hezekiah appointed several men to help Conaniah and his brother Shimei manage the supplies. Those men were Jehiel, Azaziah, Nahath, Asahel, Jerimoth, Jozabad, Eliel, Ismakiah, Mahath and Benaiah.

Kore son of Imnah, a Levite who guarded the east gate of the temple courtyard, was in charge of the contributions that people made voluntarily to God. He distributed to the priests their portion of the thanksgiving offerings and the parts of sacrifices that only they could eat.

Several Levites helped him distribute the contributions to priests and Levites who were in other cities and towns. They were Eden, Miniamin, Jeshua, Shemaiah, Amariah and Shecaniah. They distributed them honestly to those groups of priests and Levites. They did not give greater amounts to more important people.

However, they did not distribute food for any males in priestly families when they came to Jerusalem to serve in the temple. Hezekiah had organized the priests back into groups based on their ancestry to perform certain duties as their daily work. Their sons who were at least three years old accompanied them.

(Hezekiah had organized the priests by ancestry based on their clans.) Those Levites also did not distribute food to Levites who were at least 20 years old who were performing the duties of their groups.

But they did distribute food to the families of the priests and Levites whom Hezekiah had organized by ancestry. This included their wives, their younger sons, and their daughters. They distributed food to the priests’ and Levites’ entire families. They did that because the priests and Levites were faithfully devoting themselves to the work at the temple.

Some {legitimate} priests who were descendants of Aaron lived in in the pasturelands around the cities of Judah. Hezekiah appointed specific men in each city to distribute food to all the men who were priests. They also distributed food to all the men who could show that they were Levites by ancestry.
Hezekiah did this kind of thing throughout Judah. He did things that Yahweh his God considered to be good, right, and honest.

Hezekiah undertook many things in order to honor God. He restored the worship at the temple, and he obeyed the commandments in the law. He did all of these things wholeheartedly. As a result, he was successful.

After King Hezekiah had done these things so loyally to Yahweh, King Sennacherib of Assyria led his army to invade Judah. He besieged the cities that had walls around them. He thought that he would capture those cities.
Hezekiah learned that Sennacherib had invaded Judah, and he recognized that he intended to attack Jerusalem.

So he discussed with his officers and soldiers what they should do. They agreed that plenty of water should not be available to the king of Assyria and his army when they got to Jerusalem. So they decided to block the springs of water that were outside the city. Many people came to help, and they blocked all the springs of water. As a result, the Gihon stream, which flowed through that area, dried up.

Then Hezekiah strengthened Jerusalem’s defenses. He had his workers repair the sections of the city wall that had damage. He also had them repair the outer wall and the defensive towers on the main walls. He had them strengthen the Millo on the east side of the City of David. He also had them make a large number of weapons and shields.

Hezekiah appointed army commanders to direct groups of people in Jerusalem {to defend the city}. He asked the people to gather in the square inside one of the city gates so that he could speak to them. He encouraged them by saying,
“Be very brave. Do not be at all afraid of the king of Assyria, even though he has a huge army with him. Recognize that Yahweh is helping us, and his power is much greater than their power.
They have only human strength, but we have Yahweh our God helping us and fighting battles for us.” The people became more confident because of what Hezekiah, the king of Judah, told them.

Then Sennacherib sent some of his officers to Jerusalem with a message for King Hezekiah and the people of Judah who lived in Jerusalem or who had gone there for protection. Sennacherib and his army were besieging the city of Lachish at the time. But his messengers said,
“Sennacherib, the king of Assyria, says that you should not stay in Jerusalem and try to defend yourselves against his army. You should not believe that you can do that successfully.
Hezekiah is telling you that Yahweh your God will rescue you from my power. But what he says is not true. If you believe him, you will die from having no food to eat and no water to drink.

{Yahweh will not help} Hezekiah{, because he} has commanded his servants to destroy the hilltop shrines and altars where you could have worshiped Yahweh. He has told you people who live in Jerusalem and other places in Judah that you must worship and offer sacrifices only at the altar in the temple courtyard.

You must certainly know what I and the kings who ruled Assyria before me have done to the people of other countries. Certainly none of the gods that they worshiped were able to rescue them from our power. The kings who ruled before me completely destroyed many nations, and you cannot name a single god that those nations worshiped that was able to rescue them from their power. So you should not believe that your God will be able to rescue you from my power.

So do not believe what Hezekiah is telling you. If you do, he will deceive you into doing the wrong thing. Recognize that no god of any nation or kingdom has been able to rescue his people from my power or from the power of the kings who ruled Assyria before me. So your God will certainly not be able to rescue you from my power!”
Sennacherib’s officers said more bad things about Yahweh, the true God, and about Hezekiah, the king who served him loyally.

King Sennacherib also wrote letters to insult Yahweh, the God of the Israelites. He said bad things about him. He wrote, “No god of any nation anywhere else has rescued his people from my power. In the same way, the God of Hezekiah will not rescue his people from my power.”

The officers {who had come to Jerusalem} shouted in the Hebrew language to people who were standing on the city wall. They were trying to make them very afraid {so they would not fight well and} the army of Assyria would capture the city.
They talked about the God whose temple was in Jerusalem the way they talked about the gods that people worshiped in other countries. But those gods were just idols that people had made.
King Hezekiah and the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz prayed to God desperately about this.

Then Yahweh sent an angel who killed all the soldiers, officers, and commanders in the place where the army of the king of Assyria had set up its tents. This disgraced the king of Assyria, and he retreated to his own country. One day when he went into the temple of his god, some of his own sons killed him there with their swords.

That is how Yahweh rescued Hezekiah and the people of Jerusalem from the power of Sennacherib, the king of Assyria. and from the power of all their other enemies. Yahweh kept the countries around them from attacking them.
After this, the people of other nations greatly respected Hezekiah. Many people brought offerings for Yahweh to Jerusalem, and they also brought valuable gifts for King Hezekiah.

Around this time, Hezekiah became so sick that he was in danger of dying. But he prayed to Yahweh, and Yahweh told him {through the prophet Isaiah} that he would live. Yahweh gave Hezekiah a special sign to confirm this.

But Hezekiah had become very proud, so he did not make an offering at the temple to thank Yahweh for helping him. This made Yahweh angry with him and with the people who lived in Jerusalem and other places in Judah.
But then Hezekiah recognized it was wrong to be so proud, and so did the people who lived in Jerusalem. So Yahweh did not punish them during the remaining years that Hezekiah was their king.
Hezekiah became very rich, and people honored him greatly. He had his workers make storerooms for his silver, gold, precious stones, spices, shields, and other valuable things.

He also had them build buildings to store the grain, wine, and olive oil that his lands produced. He also had them make stalls for the various kinds of cattle he owned and pens for his flocks of sheep.
God enabled him to acquire so much livestock that he had his workers build enclosures where he could safely keep his large flocks of sheep and herds of cattle.

Hezekiah was the one who had his workers block the higher place where the water was flowing out of the Gihon spring and build a tunnel to bring the water {into the city} on the west side of the City of David. Hezekiah successfully completed all of his projects.

But as a result, God wanted to know what kind of person Hezekiah had become. To find out, God did not influence him to respond in a certain way when the rulers of Babylon sent messengers to him. They sent them to ask about the miracle that God had performed in the land of Judah.

The book in which the kings of Judah and Israel recorded what happened during their reigns describes further things that Hezekiah did and how he remained faithful to Yahweh. The prophet Isaiah son of Amoz wrote this account of his reign.

When Hezekiah died, the Judeans buried him near the tombs where they had buried the previous kings who were descendants of David. People who lived in Jerusalem and throughout the kingdom of Judah honored him when he died. His son Manasseh became the next king.
Manasseh was 12 years old when he began to rule. He ruled Judah for 55 years in Jerusalem.
He did many things that Yahweh considered to be evil. He imitated the disgusting practices of the nations that Yahweh had forced to leave the land of Canaan so that the Israelites could settle there.

His father Hezekiah had destroyed the shrines where the Judeans had worshiped on the tops of hills. But Manasseh commanded his workers to rebuild those shrines. He had his workers build altars for Baal. He also had them set up poles for the worship of the goddess Asherah. Manasseh also bowed down to the sun, moon, and stars to worship them.

He directed his workers to build altars {for worshiping foreign gods} and to put them inside Yahweh’s temple, even though Yahweh had said, “Jerusalem will always be the place where people worship me.”
He also had his workers make altars for the sun, moon, and stars and put them in the courtyards for the priests and the people in the temple area.

He even burned his own sons as sacrifices to false gods. He did that in the Valley of Ben Hinnom. He also performed rituals and looked for omens to try to predict the future, and he practiced sorcery. He allowed people to dig pits so they could use them try to contact people who had died. People also used those pits to try to talk to spirits that they thought could tell them things that people otherwise could not know. He did very many things that Yahweh considered to be evil, and that made Yahweh very angry.

He placed inside the temple building the image he had made that represented a false god. That was the place about which God had said to David and his son Solomon, “I will make Jerusalem, and especially this temple, places where people will always worship me. I chose Jerusalem for that purpose from among all of the cities in the land of Israel.

And if the Israelite people carefully obey all my commands and all the different kinds of laws that I gave to them through Moses, I will not make them wander again. They will be able to stay in this land that I gave to their ancestors.”

But Manasseh persuaded the people who lived in Jerusalem and other places in Judah to commit sins that were even worse than the sins that the people of the nations committed whom Yahweh destroyed so that the Israelites could settle in the land of Canaan.
Yahweh sent prophets to warn Manasseh and the people of Judah, but they ignored them.

So Yahweh allowed the king of Assyria’s army commanders to lead their soldiers to attack Jerusalem. They captured Manasseh, put a hook in his nose and bronze chains on his feet, and took him to Babylon.

But there, while he was suffering, he humbled himself greatly in relationship to {Yahweh,} the God whom his ancestors had worshiped. He became loyal to Yahweh as his God and pleaded with him to help him.

When he prayed to Yahweh, Yahweh {recognized that he was sincere and} determined to help him. Yahweh did what he asked and allowed him to return to Jerusalem and rule his kingdom again. Then Manasseh realized that Yahweh is the only true God.

After Manasseh returned, he had his workers strengthen the outer wall around Jerusalem and make it much higher. The section they strengthened extended from the west side of the Gihon spring in the valley to the Fish Gate and around the {hill of} Ophel. Manasseh also appointed army commanders for all the cities in Judah that had walls around them.

Manasseh also had his workers remove from the temple the idols that represented foreign gods and the idol that he had put there. He also had them remove all the altars that he had previously told them to build on Mount Zion, where Yahweh’s temple was, and in other places in Jerusalem. He had them throw the idols and the materials from the altars out of the city.

Then he had his workers repair Yahweh’s altar {in the temple courtyard}. He offered fellowship sacrifices on it and a special sacrifice to thank Yahweh. He told the people of Judah that they must worship only Yahweh, the God of the Israelites.
Even so, the people continued to offer sacrifices at hilltop shrines, but they offered them only to Yahweh their God.

The book in which the kings of Israel recorded what happened during their reigns describes further things that Manasseh did. These things include the messages that prophets spoke to him on behalf of Yahweh, the God of the Israelites, and Manasseh’s prayer to God {for mercy when the Babylonians captured him}.

The account that the prophet Hozai made of Manasseh’s reign records the serious sins that he committed. It lists the places where he built hilltop shrines for wooden images that represented the goddess Asherah and for other idols. But this account also describes how Manasseh then humbled himself and prayed to God and how God did what he asked.
When Manasseh died, the Judeans buried him in his palace. His son Amon became the next king.
Amon was 22 years old when he became king, and he ruled in Jerusalem for two years.

He did many things that Yahweh considered to be evil, as his father Manasseh had done {in the first part of his reign}. Manasseh’s workers had made many idols, and Amon sacrificed to them and worshiped them.
Amon did not humble himself in relationship to Yahweh as his father had done. Instead, he was even more sinful than his father had been.
Amon’s officials made a secret plan to kill him. They assassinated him in his palace.
But the people of Judah then executed all those who had assassinated Amon. They appointed his son Josiah to be the next king.
Josiah was 8 years old when he became the king of Judah. He ruled from Jerusalem for 31 years.
He did things that Yahweh considered to be right. He lived as his ancestor King David had lived. He did not live any differently.

After he had been ruling for almost eight years, while he was still a boy, he began to worship God sincerely, as his ancestor King David had done. Four years later, he began to make Jerusalem and the rest of the kingdom of Judah acceptable places to worship Yahweh. He did that by destroying the hilltop shrines where there were wooden images that represented the goddess Asherah, metal images, and other kinds of idols.

He personally accompanied his workers as they destroyed the altars where people worshiped Baal. There were idols representing the sun above those altars, and the workers cut them down. They smashed the wooden poles that represented the goddess Asherah, the metal images, and the other kinds of idols. They ground them into powder and spread the powder over the graves of the people who had offered sacrifices to those false gods.

They burned the bones of the priests who had offered sacrifices to those gods on the altars they had used to do that. That is how Josiah made Jerusalem and the rest of the kingdom of Judah acceptable places to worship Yahweh once again.

Then he went with his workers to the cities in the territories of the tribes of Manasseh, Ephraim, and Simeon. They went as far north as the territory of the tribe of Naphtali. The enemies of the Israelites had attacked and ruined the cities throughout those areas.

Josiah’s workers also destroyed the altars to foreign gods in those places. They broke apart the wooden poles that represented the goddess Asherah, and they ground the idols to powder.
